subject: BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER function
notes:
ADVERSARIAL PASS 2 - I tried to overturn this and could not; the CONFORMS is upheld on evidence I generated myself, not on the prior report. SCOPE OF THE CLAIM (stated so this row cannot be misread as 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER is done'): per scripts/spec/extract_rule_catalog.py, an FMT row is 'the unit of verify this diagram against the grammar rule that implements it' - it is the SYNTAX question only. The SEMANTICS of this function DIVERGE; see RV-15.13.4-1, which is DIVERGES on three independent sites.

(a) TRANSCRIPTION - I did not take the prior report's word for it. I extracted the PDF text layer independently (specs-private/ISO+IEC+1989-2023..., 0-based page 851 = printed folio 822) AND RENDERED THE PAGE IMAGE at 300 dpi (scripts/render-spec-page.py 852) because the standing rule is that OCR'd DIAGRAMS were systematically lossy toward falsely-restrictive syntax. The rendered diagram reads 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER ( argument-1  argument-2 )' with FUNCTION and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER UNDERLINED and nothing else underlined, NO brackets, NO braces, NO ellipsis, one Format only. specs/ISO_COBOL.md line 30217 is faithful. §15.13.2 validated with scripts/spec/cite.py --check.

(b) ACCEPTANCE - every case below re-run by ME on src/WiseOwl.Cobol.Cli/bin/Debug/net10.0/cobol.exe at --std 2023, all yielding 00000101: space-only '(5 8)'; comma '(5, 8)'; semicolon '(5; 8)'; spaces inside the parens '( 5 8 )'; identifier arguments '(IV LN)'; arithmetic-expression argument '(IV - 0, LN)'; SUBSCRIPTED argument '(E(2), 8)'; nested function argument '(FUNCTION INTEGER(5.2), 8)'; and the two forms the prior report did NOT test, which were my best shot at breaking it - SPACE-SEPARATED PARENTHESIZED arguments '((2 + 3) (4 * 2))' and a data-name-headed expression followed by a space-separated parenthesized argument '(N + 0 (4 + 4))', both of which stress the FNARG_SEPARATOR / SUBSCRIPT-mode boundary described in the CobolExpressions.g4 comment. Both accept correctly. Also verified: a USER DATA ITEM NAMED 'BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER' coexists with 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8)' in the same program and both resolve correctly (the intrinsic-function-name is not wrongly reserved); the format binds in a STRING sending position; and the §8.4.3.2.3 SR2 FUNCTION-omitted form under 'REPOSITORY. FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER INTRINSIC.' works.

(c) REJECTION (the diagram's other half - no bracket means no other arity is legal): 0, 1 and 3 arguments and the bare no-parenthesis form all reject with COBOL1504 'FUNCTION BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER takes 2 argument(s); n given (ISO 15.3)', emitted in IntrinsicBinder.BindIntrinsicCore off the IntrinsicCatalog Fixed(2,2) row; OMITTED in an argument position rejects with COBOL1544 (§8.4.3.2 SR7). All four re-run by me.

(d) EDITIONS - NOT taken from the IntrinsicCatalog row (I verified that independently of the code). Annex E of the 2023 standard is the SUBSTANTIVE CHANGES list 'between the previous COBOL standard and this Working Draft' (i.e. 2014 -> 2023) and BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER appears nowhere in it - its only post-Annex-E occurrence in specs/ISO_COBOL.md is the Index entry - so 2014 and 2023 are identical. The 85 exclusion is EXTERNAL knowledge, honestly flagged: the 2023 text carries no introduction-edition statement, and the COBOL-85 + 1989 intrinsic-function amendment set of 42 functions contains no boolean function (boolean/bit data - PICTURE 1, USAGE BIT, B"..." literals - is a COBOL-2002 addition, and §15.13.1 makes this function's type boolean).

(e) test-needed (partial). tests/conformance/2002/intrinsics_boolean_conv.cob exists on disk, is registered in tests/conformance/2002/manifest.json AND in tests/Legacy.Tests.Integration/ConformanceTests.cs, and is spec-derived (expected values hand-derived from §15.13.4 r1 and the Annex D.10 544 -> low-6-bits example - not a characterization/nist/legacy asset); I re-ran it through the CLI and it reproduces its golden exactly. It covers the format POSITIVELY and only in the comma-separated style. The SPACE-separated form as actually printed in the diagram, and the whole wrong-arity/OMITTED rejection half, appear in NO test asset (COBOL1504 and COBOL1544 are in no test) - those halves rest on my manual CLI runs above.

(f) CHECKED AND CORRECTLY OUT OF SCOPE (I re-tested the prior report's two dismissals rather than accepting them). (i) 'MOVE BOOLEAN-OF-INTEGER(5, 8) TO B8' with NO REPOSITORY entry compiles silently and dies at run time with an UNHANDLED NotImplementedCobolFeatureException instead of a bind-time 'undefined data item'. This is NOT a §15.13.2 leniency: I ran the control 'MOVE ZZ-UNDEFINED-THING(5, 8) TO B8' and 'MOVE UPPER-CASE("abc") TO B8' and BOTH are equally undiagnosed, so the missing diagnostic is the generic undefined-subscripted-reference gap, not this function's. (ii) Reference modification of a function-identifier is a parse error for UPPER-CASE too, so it is a §8.4.3.1.2 / §8.4.3.2 diagram gap, i.e. a different FMT row.
